# One-Pager Template (business summary)

Audience: SLT, executives, and teams outside the build. They decide from this page and do not read the PRD. Hold it to one page, about 350 words. If a point needs a second page, it belongs in the PRD. The test of a finished one-pager: a reader can say yes or no without opening anything else.

Writing rules that apply here: the first two sentences state the decision being asked for. Numbers over adjectives. Every recommendation names its cost. Mark unknowns as [TBD] with an owner rather than filling them in.

---

# [Initiative name]

**Owner:** [name] · **Date:** [date] · **Decision needed by:** [date] · **PRD:** [link]

## Decision needed

[Two sentences. What you are asking the reader to approve, fund, or decide, and by when.]

## The problem

[One paragraph with the number: hours, dollars, students, districts, or defects. Define any acronym on first use.]

## The bet

[One sentence: what we build or change, and for whom.]

## Outcome

[The OST item this serves, linked, plus the metric and its target. Example: OST-123, save 5 hours of analyst time per week.]

## Cost

[Team, effort, and timeline. Include the non-obvious costs: dependencies on other teams, infrastructure to stand up, migrations, support load.]

## Risks and trade-offs

[What this could break, what we give up, and what is uncertain. Two to four items, one sentence each.]

## Not doing

[The scope boundary. What people will assume is included but is not, and where each item lands later if it lands at all.]

## Status

[Where the work stands today: not started, prototype, in build, shipped. Link the prototype or demo if one exists.]
